title: Propagate termination during cloud tool bootstrap
description:
## Problem

The bootstrap INT/TERM trap cleans state but does not terminate the script, allowing a canceled run to report success.

## Steps to Reproduce

Use a disposable tools/cache root with a fake pinned Go executable that delays the first run. Send SIGTERM only to the bootstrap shell while the fake child is active, then allow the child to finish.

## Expected Behavior

The bootstrap exits nonzero, does not run later verification, keeps its lock while child work remains active, and cleans up after termination.
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic fake Go command is signaled through a test that sends INT or TERM only to the bootstrap shell while the foreground child is active. The bootstrap must terminate with nonzero status, must not begin later verification, must retain the lock while work remains active, and must remove the lock after child cleanup.
close_reason: Signal/deadline cleanup for bootstrap child processes and helper groups, with regression coverage, merged in PR #19 at main commit 197ba24596d105971b4d0d88b2dfab3edd724156 after all 9 required checks passed. This closes only the cancellation bug; the parent bootstrap task remains open.

title: Bound bootstrap subprocess output capture
description:
## Goal

Assess whether bootstrap child-process output capture needs a byte ceiling, and if so define bounded capture behavior that preserves exit classification and redaction.

## Findings

The 2026-10-12 review found `CombinedOutput` calls in installation and version-check paths, which retain child output in memory. No output-flood experiment or incident was observed; normal tools and modules are checksum/version verified. Treat this as an optional resource-hardening hypothesis, not a measured failure.
acceptance_criteria: Use bounded synthetic child output to show capture is capped or truncated. Small success and failure output keep their current classification; diagnostics reveal no child output, credentials, or environment secrets.

title: Keep pinned bootstrap source durable
description:
## Problem
The no-checkout bootstrap uses source revision `8f0072c885fad7811635523ced39df0f1a23ca33` and archive SHA-256 `02b9f1ead8dab1218bea9be434f5d501fb9c1dc7fb5ddb39732c777df3dcf6f1`, but the source revision is absent from ordinary current branch/tag refs. No current fetch outage is known. GitHub archive availability for an unreferenced object is not a durable source-lifecycle guarantee.

## Steps to Reproduce
From a clean environment with no repository checkout, run the bootstrap source acquisition against the pinned archive and digest. Repeat with a missing source and with bytes tampered while keeping the old digest.

## Expected Behavior
The exact source remains reachable through a durable ordinary branch/tag or immutable artifact without rewriting shared history. A fresh no-checkout install builds only after verifying the exact archive SHA-256; missing or modified bytes fail closed before execution. Preserve HTTPS-only acquisition and existing network/isolation policy.

Record separately the full contained source revision and full 40-character storage commit; validate the expected repository and source-revision-derived artifact path, and reject mutable branch/tag URLs, generated archive URLs, and storage-revision mismatches. Keep the raw URL, source revision, storage revision, SHA-256, and exact byte size synchronized across shell, root and embedded manifests, tests, and docs. Prove a fresh no-checkout install from verified raw bytes plus repeat/verify behavior; missing or unreachable sources and wrong-size or wrong-hash bytes must fail closed before extraction or build.

title: Scope statement/invoice table remediation experiment
description:
## Decision

Statements and invoices with tables are the first remediation priority, with neither family ranked ahead of the other. Define a finite, versioned synthetic experiment protocol. This is a configuration issue only; it does not authorize production handling or repair implementation.

## Declared engineering parameters

- One small synthetic statement transaction table and one small synthetic invoice line-item table, with equal priority.
- A fixture-authored semantic map identifies the exact target header-to-cell association. The attempted repair changes only that declared relationship and preserves every other declared association and order.
- Preserve all displayed financial strings exactly. No calculation, normalization, or invented tax, currency, date, rounding, or other arithmetic policy.
- Fixed language, font, values, and topology are experiment parameters only, not production defaults, restrictions, or a general support promise.
- Define expected proceed, reject, and inconclusive outcomes, including amount-change and association controls, malformed/unsupported inputs, ambiguous maps, cancellation, partial output, audit failure, and missing evidence.
- Keep the accepted Go-first and permissive product-dependency rules, explicit PDF/UA-2 target, and isolated CI-only veraPDF boundary. Select no writer, generation profile, production workflow, or runtime exception.

## Evidence responsibilities

`dap-jo9.2.1.2` owns actual fixture bytes, source hashes, provenance, independent baselines, and normative/control verification. `dap-jo9.1.2` owns attempted repair, candidate outputs, candidate-bound `ua2` reports, bounded outcome evidence, and the feasibility disposition. This issue owns only the reviewed protocol and declared experiment parameters.

## Rationale

A finite pair of synthetic fixtures makes the accepted statement-and-invoice remediation priority testable while keeping experiment parameters separate from product decisions.

## Alternatives Considered

Neither statement-only nor invoice-only precedence is selected. Universal font, language, topology, or financial-document support is not the first experiment. Production defaults, arithmetic policy, sensitive-document handling, reviewer authority, writer selection, and generation decisions remain outside this configuration issue.
acceptance_criteria: This issue completes when the versioned synthetic experiment protocol, declared engineering parameters, expected outcomes, and evidence responsibilities are reviewed. Actual fixture bytes, hashes, baselines, and normative-control verification belong to dap-jo9.2.1.2; attempted repair, candidate outputs, ua2 reports, and feasibility disposition belong to dap-jo9.1.2. None is required to close this configuration issue. Both statement and invoice families remain equally prioritized, and no production defaults are selected.
notes:
Accepted priority: statements and invoices with tables matter first and most. Proposed finite next experiment for a later batch only: two small synthetic fixtures (a statement transaction table and invoice line-item table); test one explicitly mapped table-header relationship repair by an eligible Go-first candidate. Preserve displayed strings exactly (dates, signs, decimals, currency, quantities, totals); perform no arithmetic recalculation. First verify the exact normative representation and validator positive/negative controls. Require an actual structure change, independent immutable input baseline, separate atomic candidate, independent cell/header/row association predicate, candidate-hash-bound explicit ua2 CI evidence, metadata-change disclosure, amount and association mutation controls, and review-needed/unsupported/fail-safe outcomes for ambiguity, unsupported topology, missing evidence, cancellation, and partial writes. End proceed/reject/inconclusive for this operation; no-go is valid. Partially tagged PDF 2.0 may isolate editing capability but implies no PDF 1.7-to-2.0, arbitrary untagged, multi-page/merged-table, or general financial-document support. These are experimental assumptions, not production scope. Real-document language/topology, operator mapping acceptability, production handling, and reviewer authority remain open. No implementation is authorized in batch one.
See [Decision 0002](docs/decisions/0002-initial-remediation-family-priority.md). Family priority is accepted in Decision 0002. This issue remains open for the unresolved experiment-profile and acceptance criteria. Its open status does not revoke the accepted priority.
Protocol follow-up after independent review: now records the required sorted /StructTreeRoot /IDTree mapping to actual TH elements, reproducible external text/render observations, actual MCID/ParentTree/Pg/P verification ownership, and whole-document limitations. Configuration-only experiment scope remains unchanged.

Versioned equal-priority statement/invoice scope, experiment parameters, expected outcomes, pre-repair controls, evidence ownership, and production boundaries are explicit. title: Keep generation profile separate from remediation
description:
## Decision

Keep accessible-document generation as a separate lane with its own profile, family choices, semantic requirements, and engine decision. The remediation priority does not decide any generation profile value.

The existing plan separates generation from existing-PDF remediation; preserving that boundary avoids making generation decisions prerequisites for the first remediation experiment.

Sharing the remediation profile or treating the statement/invoice priority as a generation-family selection is not adopted. No generation family or engine is selected by this issue.

title: Resolve production document handling gates
description:
## Decision

Production document handling remains Open. Keep this gate scoped to real or sensitive documents and production processing; it does not block synthetic engineering. Do not use private/real documents or claim production readiness until the applicable decisions are made.

## Rationale

Access, confidentiality, retention/deletion, and diagnostic redaction need an authorized owner decision when such handling becomes material. Synthetic fixtures do not establish production defaults.

## Alternatives Considered

No default retention, deletion, access, or redaction policy is assumed. A blanket production-policy prerequisite for all synthetic feasibility work is not adopted; sensitive/production use remains gated.
acceptance_criteria: Record the authorized owner and evidence for input confidentiality, access, storage, retention/deletion, and diagnostic redaction decisions; otherwise retain each item as Open and explicitly gate production/sensitive-document processing. Do not introduce real/private documents, enable retention, or claim production readiness.

## Goal

Run a bounded, test-first feasibility investigation for the versioned synthetic operation configured by `dap-jo9.1.1.1`, using actual fixture bytes, hashes, independent baselines, and normative/control verification supplied by `dap-jo9.2.1.2`. This issue covers the attempted repair and independently reviewed finite disposition; it does not select a production writer or approve unrelated profiles or product scope.

## Repair-spike entry

Begin an actual repair attempt only after both A fixtures and immutable baselines are available, the declared normative representation and validator controls are verified, and `dap-jo9.1.3` records permissive-license/capability clearance for the exact proposed candidate and its reachable materials. A missing prerequisite is evidence for an inconclusive disposition, not permission to fabricate an output.

## Proceed evidence

For both fixtures, make an actual declared header-to-cell relationship change, preserve the original bytes and exact displayed financial strings, preserve all non-target declared relations/order, produce a separate atomic candidate, compare independently, and bind explicit `ua2` CI reports and metadata disclosures to the candidate hash. Include amount and association mutations, positive/negative validator controls, and bounded failure controls for malformed, unsupported, ambiguous, cancelled, partial-write, and audit-failure outcomes.

## Reject or inconclusive evidence

A reject or inconclusive result requires evidence of the bounded attempted steps, the exact failure or missing prerequisite, applicable limits, and the next decision. Do not invent a candidate, output, validator report, or successful repair when a prerequisite is missing or a step fails. A no-go is valid.

## Completion boundary

Independent acceptance of the finite proceed/reject/inconclusive disposition completes this issue. It does not select a production writer, expand supported scope, close unrelated profile/product gates, establish release eligibility, or claim human/AT approval. A no-op PDF 1.7 write is insufficient. Partially tagged PDF 2.0 can isolate editing capability but proves neither PDF 1.7 conversion nor arbitrary untagged/complex-table support. Preserve the explicit PDF/UA-2 target, Go-first approach, permissive product rule, and isolated CI-only veraPDF exception.

Reject or inconclusive requires bounded attempted-step evidence, the exact failure or missing prerequisite, limits, and the next decision, with no invented output or validator report. Independent review and acceptance of the finite disposition completes dap-jo9.1.2. title: Decide traceability checker scaling threshold or monitor mode (with owner and re-check trigger)
description:
## Goal

Retain verified scaling evidence for the traceability checker pending product triage. Record an explicit threshold decision — either a (size, runtime-budget) pair with the growth assumption and review date that justify it, or an explicit "no threshold adopted — monitor mode" statement — plus the owner and the trigger condition for re-checking. Any adopted (size, runtime-budget) threshold pair is tooling-triage housekeeping, not a product performance budget.

## Findings (controlled rerun, 2026-10-13)

Provenance: Go 1.27.2, linux/amd64; the run used -cpu=1 (GOMAXPROCS=1; NumCPU=5 is the machine's CPU count). Five raw repetitions retained in docs/research/support/traceability-scaling-benchmark-2026-10-13.txt.

Current catalog (17 requirements, 6 stories, 21 tasks, 26 cases): 0.526 ms Validate, 0.107 ms GeneratedMarkdown.

Synthetic one-to-one catalogs (uniform linkage between entity types; see the linkage-density caveat in Notes):

| entities | Validate (median) | GeneratedMarkdown (median) |
|----------|-------------------|----------------------------|
| 100      | 0.557 ms          | 0.464 ms                   |
| 1,000    | 19.896 ms         | 21.196 ms                  |
| 5,000    | 441.795 ms        | 495.460 ms                 |

Fitted growth exponents: Validate ~1.55 (100→1,000) and ~1.93 (1,000→5,000); GeneratedMarkdown ~1.66 and ~1.96. Growth is near-quadratic above ~1,000 entities and sub-quadratic below; the exponent itself varies with n, so any extrapolated threshold is regime-dependent. Each 5,000-entity repetition is a single benchmark iteration (N=1); only five repetitions exist, so the worst-case medians rest on a thin sample.

This is a scaling signal, not a current performance incident. No optimization was performed.

## Superseded (exploratory, 2026-10-12)

The 2026-10-12 exploratory run (repository-backed medians 0.464 ms Validate, 0.112 ms GeneratedMarkdown; synthetic medians 0.524/19.389/423.537 ms Validate and 0.473/20.426/482.676 ms GeneratedMarkdown at 100/1,000/5,000 entities) is superseded and is not the controlled comparison baseline: complete toolchain/runner provenance was not captured contemporaneously, and the original Go test output used the default test CPU setting.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A recorded threshold decision: either a (size, runtime-budget) pair with the growth assumption and review date that justify it, or an explicit "no threshold adopted — monitor mode" statement.
2. A named owner and a trigger condition for re-checking (e.g. catalog exceeds N entities or Validate exceeds X ms), plus a review-by date.
3. If indexing is ever proposed: unchanged diagnostics and no unintended change to generated Markdown views (byte-identical against the pre-indexing baseline, which must be named at proposal time), plus repeated benchmarks showing flatter growth — "materially" means fitted exponent < 1.5 on the 1,000→5,000-entity interval — with no allocation regression against the 5,000-entity baseline (8,452,576 B/op, 40,247 allocs/op per docs/research/support/traceability-scaling-benchmark-2026-10-13.txt).

## Goal

Simulated unit-test outcomes must be labeled as simulations and must never be reported as a human or assistive-technology pass. title: Select authoritative approver-role evidence source and temporal policy
description:
## Problem

Decision 0004 designates the approver-user persona but does not identify an authoritative, time-aware source that can prove a person held that role at `reviewed_at`. An identity string or self-asserted role is insufficient. PR #71 P1 review finding: https://github.com/pratik-saptarshi/document-accessibility-pipeline/pull/71#discussion_r4277123170

## Rationale

The release gate must distinguish the accepted approver role from the evidence proving that a particular person held it when a review occurred. Without a trusted historical authority source, the gate cannot safely validate an approval or its validity interval. A digest can identify evidence bytes but cannot authenticate the issuer or establish role authority.

## Owner decision required

The product owner must select a trusted source and verification interface, identity mapping, and policy for grant validity, expiry, revocation, and retroactive authorization. The selected source must make authorization evidence verifiable at the UTC `reviewed_at` timestamp and provide an immutable reference that can be checked again at release.

## Alternatives Considered

- An owner-approved append-only role-grant register.
- A named organizational identity and access-control system.

Neither alternative is selected or approved by this issue. The source, interface, validity-window behavior, retroactivity, and revocation semantics remain open.

## Acceptance criteria

- A product-owner accepted decision names the trusted source/interface and specifies how identity, approver role, and source authenticity are verified.
- The decision defines the validity interval semantics at the UTC `reviewed_at` time and the effect of expiry, revocation, retroactive grants, unavailable source, and replaced evidence.
- An immutable authorization evidence reference and digest can be retained and re-verified at release; self-asserted identity or role labels are rejected.
- Negative-test specifications require rejection of operator-only, unknown, unauthorized, expired, not-yet-valid, malformed/time-invalid, missing, unverifiable, wrong-source, identity/role-mismatched, replaced, forged, and digest-mismatched evidence.
- The trusted-role-verification task `dap-jo9.2.5.9.2` remains blocked by this owner decision until it is accepted and the implementation contract can verify the selected source. Authority-independent synthetic evidence-contract cases are tracked separately in `dap-jo9.2.5.9.1`; no source or authority is inferred from simulations or machine results.

## Scope limits

This issue records an owner decision and testable contract, not a provider integration, authentication mechanism, or human-review implementation. Keep the accepted history of `dap-jo9.1.1.4` and Decision 0004 intact. Do not claim human or assistive-technology acceptance.
acceptance_criteria: Record a product-owner accepted, testable decision for trusted time-aware role evidence and validity/revocation semantics; preserve no-source-is-selected status until accepted.

title: Verify authoritative approver-role evidence at review time
description:
## Goal

Implement trusted approver-role evidence verification for the candidate-bound semantic and assistive-technology review gate, using only the source and temporal/revocation policy accepted in `dap-jo9.1.1.6`.

## Required behavior

Verify that authoritative, immutable source evidence binds the acting identity to the approver role and that the grant was valid at the review's UTC `reviewed_at`. Retain a source reference and digest that can be re-verified at release. Reject self-asserted roles and operator-only, unknown, unauthorized, expired, not-yet-valid, malformed/time-invalid, missing, unverifiable, wrong-source, identity/role-mismatched, replaced, forged, or digest-mismatched evidence. Apply the accepted expiry, revocation, retroactivity, and source-unavailability policy; otherwise fail closed to blocked/review-needed.

Use source-specific fakes or fixtures only to test verification mechanics. Such tests are simulations and never constitute genuine semantic or AT acceptance. Do not add an authority provider, authentication mechanism, secrets, permission changes, or non-Go runtime without required product/security decisions and approval.

## Dependency and boundary

This task is blocked by the owner decision `dap-jo9.1.1.6`. The authority-independent synthetic record-contract task is tracked separately at `dap-jo9.2.5.9.1`. The parent gate cannot close until both work slices and its actual eligible-candidate evidence criteria pass.

## Definition of done

Test the accepted source-specific policy and every listed negative case, including authority validity exactly at `reviewed_at`, expiry, revocation, retroactive grants, unavailable source, and immutable-reference replacement. Demonstrate that invalid/unverifiable authority returns blocked/review-needed and that no simulated result is surfaced as a human or AT pass. Preserve the accepted Decision 0004 protocol and canonical case ownership.
acceptance_criteria: After accepted decision dap-jo9.1.1.6, validate immutable trusted-source role evidence for the acting identity at UTC reviewed_at under its accepted validity/revocation policy; reject missing, forged, replaced, mismatched, unauthorized, operator-only, expired, not-yet-valid, and time-invalid evidence; fail closed; simulations never count as human/AT acceptance.

title: Test fail-safe publication of financial fixture pairs
description:
## Goal

Close the round-two Task 7 test-coverage gap for `internal/financialfixtures.publishV2Artifacts`. The current implementation has baseline checks, no-clobber publication, and best-effort rollback; the failure outcomes need direct deterministic tests. This issue treats the concern as a coverage gap, not a confirmed production defect.

## Findings

The review plan identified missing direct failure-injection coverage for fixture staging, second-file publication, rollback, read-back, and existing-target preservation. The current publisher writes the four allowlisted v2 outputs for statement and invoice positive/damaged fixtures.

## Scope

Use only synthetic byte payloads and isolated temporary directories to exercise the exact four v2 publication targets as one publication set. Keep this test-first and narrowly scoped to `internal/financialfixtures`; introduce only private injectable operations justified by deterministic fault injection. No tracked fixture PDFs or baselines may be altered.

## Acceptance

Demonstrate the relevant test failing against the pre-fix behavior before implementing the smallest required change. Include success and injected-failure controls for the publication invariants below. A failure must never be reported as successful or leave a mixed set treated as complete. A rollback failure must be reported honestly with the residual state; do not claim filesystem atomicity or successful rollback when cleanup failed.

Source review: [round-two review plan, Task 7](docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-15-round-two-review-validation-and-plan.md) and [round-three quality follow-up, section E](docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-16-round-three-quality-follow-up.md).
acceptance_criteria:
1. In disposable temporary directories with synthetic bytes, a staging failure leaves all four publication targets unchanged or absent and removes staged temporary files.
2. Inject failure on the second file publication after the first new target is published. When rollback succeeds, the publisher returns a non-success error, removes only files created by that attempt, and preserves every preexisting target byte-for-byte.
3. Inject rollback failure separately. The publisher returns a non-success error that reports both the publication and rollback failures; tests verify and document any residual new file without claiming the pair was rolled back or successfully published. All preexisting known-good targets remain byte-identical.
4. Verify each newly published target by reading it back and comparing exact expected bytes or their planned digest before returning success. Inject read-back error and byte mismatch; each returns non-success and performs best-effort cleanup of only newly created targets while preserving preexisting target bytes.
5. Cover identical preexisting targets as a preserving success/control, conflicting preexisting targets as preflight rejection with all known-good bytes unchanged, and a target appearing after preflight as a no-clobber publication failure.
6. A deterministic successful run verifies exact bytes/digests for all four statement/invoice positive/damaged outputs and repeat generation stability. Test inputs/outputs are isolated synthetic files; SHA-256 hashes of tracked v1/v2 fixture baselines remain unchanged and no tracked PDF is edited.
7. Tests are test-first and mutation-sensitive to unsafe success, skipped read-back, target overwrite, and rollback omissions. Run `go test -race ./internal/financialfixtures`; if production code changes, run all repository-prescribed root/nested checks and exact-head CI. No Java/veraPDF execution locally.
8. Keep changes limited to this fixture publication contract and its tests. Bootstrap `run()` CLI tests, repair implementation, new fixture content, production support claims, and human/AT acceptance remain out of scope.
notes: P2 follow-up for round-two Task 7, financial-fixture transaction-assurance slice only; bootstrap CLI coverage is separately scoped. Preserve existing synthetic fixture files and hashes. Do not change the live embedded Dolt store or close/update any other issue, including dap-jo9.5.6, dap-jo9.5.7, or dap-jo9.1.6.10. Any rollback limitation must be surfaced as an error and accurately described; do not promise atomic multi-file filesystem publication.
